concept.title: Development and contributing
concept.shortdesc: The plugin is open source under Apache-2.0; design decisions, requirements, and the gap analyses live alongside the code, and contributions follow the iStandUK exemplar for Git and GitHub practice.

ul.li: org.istanduk.gov-uk/ — the plugin itself: transtype declaration, Ant glue, XSLT overrides, and vendored govuk-frontend assets
design/ — the full design record: context, requirements with per-item status, architecture, component inventory, decision log, and the gap analyses against real corpora
fixtures/ — the regression fixtures exercising bookmaps, keys, chunking, the SVG domain, search semantics, and unresolved keys
tools/ — the checks continuous integration runs: link checker, page-weight budget, accessibility and print smoke scripts

conbody.p: The architecture in one sentence: a standard DITA-OT plugin whose govuk transformation extends html5, overriding only the rendering while inheriting all of the toolkit's DITA processing.
conbody.note: Issues and pull requests are welcome. Check the design folder's open questions and the issue tracker before proposing large changes — many decisions are already recorded with their rationale.

section.title: How work flows
section.p: The repository follows the branching model in the iStandUK hello-world exemplar. main holds released code only; dev is the integration branch and the default; a change starts from an issue, lives on a feature/ branch from dev, and returns through a small pull request that links the issue. Releases go from dev to main on a release/ branch and are tagged there; urgent fixes take a hotfix/ branch from main. Both long-lived branches are protected: a pull request and a green build are required, and history is never rewritten. The repository's CONTRIBUTING.md has the details, including the ground rules — vendor-neutral wording, no restricted brand assets, Node-free builds, and publisher choice with warnings rather than errors for anything that touches content risk.

section.title: What continuous integration checks
section.p: Every pull request and every push to the long-lived branches builds this manual and the fixtures across the supported DITA-OT versions, validates the HTML with the Nu validator, checks every internal link and anchor, measures page weight against the budget, runs axe-core at WCAG 2.2 AA, builds twice to prove the output is byte-identical, prints the print document to PDF in a browser, and asserts the neutral-branding guarantees — no fonts, no crown imagery, no external requests. The same checks can be run locally before opening a pull request; the commands are in CONTRIBUTING.md.

section.title: Releases
section.p: A release is cut from a release/ branch: the version is bumped in the plugin and in this manual's install topic, the branch is merged into main and tagged, the plugin zip is published as the release asset with its checksum, the install is verified from the public URL, and a new version entry is submitted to the DITA-OT plugin registry so that dita install org.istanduk.gov-uk resolves to it. The checklist is docs/RELEASING.md in the repository.

section.title: Reporting a security problem
section.p: Please report vulnerabilities privately through the repository's security advisory form rather than as a public issue; SECURITY.md gives the route, the response you can expect, and what belongs to the plugin as opposed to the toolkit, govuk-frontend or Pagefind.
